What matters when looking at phones is the radio channel. Phone towers (in the US at least) come mainly in two flavors: CDMA (Verizon & Sprint) and GSM (T-Mobile and AT&T). For your purposes, all you need to know is that CDMA phones will not work, under any circumstances, on a GSM network. You can't take a Verizon phone and use it on T-Mobile's network. When buying a phone (whether it be off Craigslist, an online retailer, or whatever), it should say somewhere on the page if it runs on CDMA or GSM, or it will have the specific carrier it is locked to. If it doesn't have this information, stay away.

A lot of the time, phones will be "locked in" to a specific carrier. If you buy a phone that is locked into AT&T's network (because it's GSM), you can "unlock" it; That is, use it on other GSM carriers like T-Mobile. The process for this varies from phone to phone, and could cost anywhere from $0-75. The unlocking process is usually pretty painless. Google is your friend here.

When buying a phone, be SURE it is a GSM phone if you're going with T-Mobile. Unlocked is always preferred, but be sure to weigh your options. If it would be cheaper buy a locked phone and unlock it yourself vs. buying an unlocked phone... well... It's up to you.

You can use any t-mobile phone with your current plan. If the phone you purchase uses a different size sim than your current phone, go to a t-mobile store (assuming your carrier is t-mobile, not an MVNO like straight talk or family mobile that uses t-mobile's network) and ask for a sim for the phone you are switching to.

I would suggest going to a Best Buy or Target to purchase a new prepaid t-mobile phone. That way you have a return policy (30 days at Target) and a legit warranty through the manufacturer. They usually have better priced prepaid than the carrier stores. If you don't need the phone immediately and want to find the best price on a device, go to slickdeals.net, set up an account and an alert for the phone you want. Black Friday is almost here and you could probably score a sweet deal.

You do have options if you want to switch to another carrier. If your plan includes unlimited talk/text for that price there are other's with better coverage for the same price. For a few bucks more unlimited everything monthly, but not the best in coverage on the prepaid side. It really depends on what you need and what works best where you are located.
